english.title: Aid / abet the driving of a motor vehicle otherwise than is accordance with a licence - non endorseable offence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to drive a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), otherwise than in accordance with a licence authorising

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

to drive a motor vehicle of that class in circumstances where

(C)_[his]_
(D)_[her]_

driving would have been in accordance with any licence that could have been granted to them, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CIRCUMSTANCES - DO NOT CONFUSE THIS OFFENCE WITH THE ENDORSEABLE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 87(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988, section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
aided / abetted / counselled / procured
a person to drive a motor vehicle on a road
not in accordance with a licence
authorising a motor vehicle of that class
This is the NON-ENDORSABLE VERSION of the offence and should BE USED:-
(a) in circumstances such as where the offender has held a full driving licence which has lapsed, for example:- the offender has forgotten to renew it or is over 70 years of age and has not re sat a test OR
(b) where the driver has had his licence to drive revoked because of a failure to surrender it for endorsement, then, provided his / her driving would have been in accordance with that licence this non endorseable offence wording should be used.
(ii) Where the offender held, or could have been granted, a driving licence authorising the driving of the vehicle in question AND he / she was driving in circumstances that were not or would not have been in accordance with that licence - that offence is liable to endorsement and officers should refer to the endorsable version at CJS Code RT88334 and H31.
(iii) The item in Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act relating to section 87(1) provides that endorsement and disqualification apply "in a case where the offender's driving would not have been in accordance with any licence that could have been granted to him".
